c.tagline: A Patagonian lakeside town whose sole purpose is being the gateway to the thundering Perito Moreno Glacier

card: Widely accepted; cash (preferably USD for exchange) useful for smaller shops

taxi.fareNote: Most visitors book a Perito Moreno tour bus rather than a taxi for the glacier itself

emergency.note: 911 is the general emergency line in most of Argentina; 107 specifically reaches medical services

walk: Central El Calafate's main street is walkable; the Perito Moreno Glacier (80km away) requires a tour bus or rental car

safety.safety: Very safe town, geared almost entirely toward tourism
safety.crime: Minimal crime; weather can affect glacier excursions

hood_landmark.Av. del Libertador (Main Street): El Calafate's main tourist strip of restaurants and tour agencies
hood_landmark.Laguna Nimez: Laguna Nimez nature reserve's flamingo colonies
hood_landmark.Perito Moreno Glacier (day-trip): The Perito Moreno Glacier's walkway viewing platforms
hood_landmark.Glaciarium Area: The Glaciarium ice museum overlooking Lago Argentino

hood_desc: The town's main commercial strip with most hotels, restaurants, and tour operators; the natural base for any visit.
A small nature reserve on the edge of town, an easy walk for birdwatching including flamingos on Lago Argentino.
The main event: a network of viewing platforms directly facing the actively calving glacier, about 1.5-2 hr from town.
A quieter lakefront stretch near downtown, popular for a sunset stroll along Lago Argentino.
A striking modern ice-and-glacier museum a short drive from town, good for context before or after visiting Perito Moreno.

water.note: Patagonian tap water is safe to drink.

transit.sys: Local minibuses and tour buses to Perito Moreno Glacier
transit.map: Not centrally published; tour agencies handle transport to the glacier
transit.note: A rental car or organized tour bus is necessary to reach Perito Moreno Glacier

transport.air: El Calafate Airport (FTE), about 15-20 min from downtown, with domestic flights from Buenos Aires and Ushuaia
transport.bus: Long-distance buses connect to El Chaltén (about 3 hr) and Rio Gallegos
transport.car: Rental cars available; National Route 11 connects to the Perito Moreno Glacier

net.m: Good 4G coverage in town, limited near the glacier
net.w: Free wifi standard in hotels and cafes
net.ap: A Movistar, Claro, or Personal tourist SIM or eSIM
